label: thm:main-non-vanishing
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: thm:main-moments
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main-moments}
For $\ell=4$ or $6$, fix an odd prime power $q\equiv-1\pmod\ell$,
and put $g=(\ell-1)(m-1)$. For every $\varepsilon>0$, uniformly in
monic $h$ with $\deg h\le m/10$,
\begin{align}\label{intro:twisted-moments}
 \sum_{\chi\in\mathcal C_\ell(g)}\chi(h)L_q(1/2,\chi)
 ={}&q^{2m}\mathcal M_{\ell,q}(h)\notag\\
 &+O_{q,\varepsilon}\!\left(
 q^{(\alpha_\ell+\varepsilon)m}
 |h_\ell^\ast|^{\beta_\ell+\varepsilon}|h|^\varepsilon\right),
\end{align}
where
\[
 (\alpha_4,\beta_4)=\left(\frac95,\frac1{10}\right),
 \qquad
 (\alpha_6,\beta_6)=\left(\frac{13}{7},\frac1{14}\right).
\]
head: environment
name: Uniform twisted first moments

label: lem:family
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:family}
The parameterization \eqref{eq:family} is one-to-one onto the primitive
order-four characters satisfying \eqref{eq:conductor-condition} and
having conductor degree $2m$.  For these characters,
\[
 \operatorname{cond}(\chi_F)=FF^\sigma,\qquad
 \chi_{F^\sigma}=\overline{\chi_F}.
\]
They are even.  The associated cyclic quartic extension has genus
$g=3m-3$, and the completed $L$-polynomial has degree $2m-2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
A base-field prime admits a local character of exact order four only
when its degree is even.  It then splits as $P=\pi\pi^\sigma$ over
$\mathbb F_{q^2}$, and the two choices $\pi$ and $\pi^\sigma$ give the two
local characters of exact order four.  Condition
\eqref{eq:conductor-condition} excludes local characters of order two
at ramified primes.  The Chinese remainder theorem now gives the claimed bijection; see
\cite[Lemma~3.6]{Lin}.

For a constant $a\in\mathbb F_q^\times$, its quartic residue symbol at a prime
of $\mathbb F_{q^2}[T]$ is one, since $q-1$ divides
$(q^{2d}-1)/4$.  Thus these characters are even.  Each finite ramified
prime has ramification index four and infinity is unramified.
Riemann--Hurwitz gives $2g-2=-8+3(2m)$, hence $g=3m-3$.
The degree of the completed Dirichlet $L$-polynomial is the conductor
degree minus two.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The parameters $F$ and $F^\sigma$ give distinct conjugate characters.
The family \eqref{eq:family} includes only characters satisfying
\eqref{eq:conductor-condition}. Its genus parameter is $3m-3$,
whereas the completed $L$-polynomial has degree $2m-2$.
head: environment

label: lem:count
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:B
title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\mu_q$ and $\mu_Q$ for the M\"obius functions over the two
fields. As in \cite[proof of Corollary~1.1]{Hong}, insert
\[
 1_{(F,F^\sigma)=1}=\sum_{\substack{D\in\mathcal A_q\\D\mid F}}\mu_q(D),
 \qquad \mu_Q^2(F)=\sum_{A^2\mid F}\mu_Q(A).
\]
For $|u|<q^{-2}$, the counting series, including $F=1$, is therefore
\begin{align}\label{eq:B}
 \sum_{\substack{F\in\mathcal A_{q^2}\text{ square-free}\\(F,F^\sigma)=1}} u^{\deg F}
 &=\sum_{D\in\mathcal A_q}\mu_q(D)u^{\deg D}
   \sum_{\substack{A,G\in\mathcal A_{q^2}\\(AG,D)=1}}
       \mu_Q(A)u^{2\deg A+\deg G}\notag\\
 &=\frac{\zeta_Q(u)}{\zeta_Q(u^2)}
   \prod_P\left(1-u^{\deg P}
       \prod_{\pi\mid P}(1+u^{\deg\pi})^{-1}\right)\notag\\
 &=\zeta_Q(u)
   \prod_{\deg P\text{ odd}}(1-u^{\deg P})
   \prod_{\deg P\text{ even}}
       (1+2u^{\deg P/2})(1-u^{\deg P/2})^2.
\end{align}
Here and below, $\pi$ denotes a monic prime over $\mathbb F_Q$.
The product multiplying $\zeta_Q(u)$ converges normally for
$|u|<q^{-1}$, since each local factor is $1+O(|u|^{\deg P})$.
Its value at $u=q^{-2}$ is $c_q$. Perron's formula and a shift to
$|u|=q^{-1-\varepsilon}$, with $0<\varepsilon<1$, give
\eqref{eq:count}. Finally, at each even-degree prime,
\[
 (1+2|P|^{-1})(1-|P|^{-1})^2\ge(1-|P|^{-2})^3;
\]
the same lower bound holds for the odd-degree factor. Multiplication
over $P$ gives \eqref{eq:cq-lower}.
head: environment

label: lem:orthog
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By quartic reciprocity, the summand is the character
$\left(\frac{R}{AB^3}\right)_4$.  It is induced modulo $\operatorname{rad}(AB)$, and the degree
condition makes monic degree-$m$ polynomials equidistributed over its
residue classes.  The induced character is principal exactly when
all the exponents in $AB^3$ are divisible by four.  Its principal
average is the proportion of invertible classes; otherwise its
average is zero.
head: environment

label: lem:model-bounds
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:model-bounds}
If $Z=\sum_Pc_PX_P$ and $V=\sum_P|c_P|^2$, then, for $t\ge0$ and
$p\ge2$,
\[
 \mathbb E e^{t\operatorname{Re} Z}\le e^{t^2V/2},\qquad
 \lVertZ\rVert_p\le4\sqrt{pV},\qquad
 \mathbb E e^{t|Z|}\le4e^{t^2V}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Each real summand has mean zero and is bounded by $|c_P|$.
Hoeffding's lemma and independence give the exponential estimate.  Its tail bound, applied to the real and
imaginary parts, gives the displayed moment estimate.  Finally
$|Z|\le|\operatorname{Re} Z|+|\Im Z|$ and summing over the four choices of signs gives
the last inequality.
head: environment

label: prop:first-factor
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $hf$ is a fourth power, $\chi_F(hf)$ is the indicator of
$(F,hf)=1$.  By Lemma~\ref{lem:count} and \eqref{eq:rho}, its generating series, multiplied by $1-q^{2-2s}$,
has value $c_q\rho(hf)$ at $s=1$.  Substitution of
\eqref{eq:first-diagonal} gives $\rho(hf)=\rho(hB)$ and the weight
$|h^\ast|^{-1/2}|B|^{-2}$.  At $P\nmid h$, the local $B$-sum is
\[
 1+\frac{\rho_P|P|^{-2}}{1-|P|^{-2}}
 =\frac{1-(1-\rho_P)|P|^{-2}}{1-|P|^{-2}},
\]
whereas at $P\mid h$ it is $\frac{\rho_P}{1-|P|^{-2}}$.
Multiplying the local factors proves \eqref{eq:Mmain-product}.
head: environment

label: lem:root-normalization
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The map
\[
 b\pmod F\longmapsto bF^\sigma+b^\sigma F\pmod{FF^\sigma}
\]
is a bijection onto the base-field residue classes: it is invariant
under $\sigma$, and is invertible by the Chinese remainder theorem.
Its additive character is $e_Q(b/F)$, while its multiplicative
character is $\chi_F(b)\chi_F(F^\sigma)$. This proves the first equality.
If $R=\operatorname{Res}_T(F,F^\sigma)$, the norm definition of the
quartic symbol gives $\chi_F(F^\sigma)=R^{(Q-1)/4}$, interpreted through
our fixed identification of roots of unity. Moreover
\[
 R^q=\operatorname{Res}_T(F^\sigma,F)=(-1)^dR.
\]
Consequently $R^{(Q-1)/4}=(-1)^{d(q+1)/4}$.
Finally, the root-number formula for a primitive even character of
conductor degree $2d$ is $q^{-d}G_q(\chi_F)$.
head: environment

label: lem:restricted-gauss
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:restricted-inclusion
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $a$ be the product of the extension-field primes dividing $h$
but not $r$. In the notation of \cite[Section~5]{DFL25}, set
\[
 \psi_r^{(i)}(r,E,v)=\frac1{1-Q^4v^4}
 \sum_{\substack{F\in\mathcal A_{q^2}\\(F,r)=1,\ E\mid F\\
                    \deg F\equiv i\ (4)}}G_Q(r,F)v^{\deg F}.
\]
Finite inclusion--exclusion gives the exact identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:restricted-inclusion}
 \widetilde\Psi_Q(r,v;h)=(1-Q^4v^4)
 \sum_{E\mid a}\mu_Q(E)\sum_{i=0}^3\psi_r^{(i)}(r,E,v).
\end{equation}
Theorem~5.3 and Corollary~5.4 of \cite{DFL25}, with base field $Q$
and order four, apply since $E$ is square-free and $(E,r)=1$.
More explicitly, write
$r=r_1r_2^2r_3^3r_4^4$, with $r_1,r_2,r_3$ square-free and pairwise
coprime, as required by the cited theorem. Its second case applies
for order $\ell=4$: throughout $1<\alpha<3/2$ one has
$4\le6/(3-2\alpha)$. The exponent of $|E|_2$ becomes
$\ell(3/4-\alpha/2)-1=2-2\alpha$, while the exponent of $|r|_2$
is $3/4-\alpha/2$. Consequently the quoted bound is
\[
 \psi_r^{(i)}(r,E,v)
 \ll |Er|_2^\epsilon |E|_2^{2-2\alpha}
                   |r|_2^{3/4-\alpha/2}.
\]
The divisor sum is bounded by
\[
 |r|_2^\epsilon\sum_{E\mid a}|E|_2^{2-2\alpha+\epsilon}
 =|r|_2^\epsilon\prod_{\pi\mid a}
                (1+|\pi|_2^{2-2\alpha+\epsilon}).
\]
Choose the preliminary $\epsilon$ smaller than $2\alpha-2$ on
the chosen closed interval. Each factor is then at most two, and
$2^{\omega(a)}\ll_{Q,\epsilon'}|a|_2^{\epsilon'}$ for every
$\epsilon'>0$: separate the finitely many primes of bounded degree
and use $2\le|\pi|_2^{\epsilon'}$ for the others.
Since $a\mid\operatorname{rad}(h)$, this proves the asserted bound
after replacing the small exponents by $\epsilon$.
The unrestricted metaplectic series satisfies
\[
 \psi^{(i)}(r,v)=\frac{v^iP_{r,i}(v^4)}{1-Q^5v^4}
\]
with $P_{r,i}$ a polynomial; see \cite[equation~(4.2)]{DFL25}.
The finite decomposition in Theorem~5.3 expresses the restricted
series through such functions and finite local factors. Its possible
poles are zeros of $1-Q^5v^4$ or of the finite denominator factors
in \cite[Theorem~5.3]{DFL25}. In the latter the quartic reciprocity
sign is one because
$Q\equiv1\pmod8$; their form is $1-Q^{3\deg\pi}v^{4\deg\pi}$.
The global factor has zeros at $|v|=Q^{-5/4}$ and the local factors
at $|v|=Q^{-3/4}$. The decomposition and \eqref{eq:restricted-inclusion} therefore give
holomorphy for $|v|<Q^{-5/4}$, with uniform bounds on compact
subannuli.
head: environment

label: input:first
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Uniform twisted first moment

title: Proof
body_md:
At $s=1$, the continuation region contains $\tau>3/8$.
Thus $\left[(1-Q^{1-s})A_4(s,w;h)\right]_{s=1}$ is holomorphic on that half-plane and
agrees, for $\tau>1$, with \eqref{eq:residue-function}.
The latter expression is holomorphic for $\tau>1/4$; the one-variable
identity theorem shows that they agree throughout $\tau>3/8$.
In particular, $[(1-Q^{1-s})A_4(s,1/2;h)]_{s=1}=\mathcal M_{4,q}(h)$.

By periodicity in $s$ and \eqref{eq:central-slice},
$A_4(u,1/2;h)$ extends meromorphically to $|u|<q^{-9/5}$.
Since $\left[(1-Q^{1-s})A_4(s,1/2;h)\right]_{s=1}=\mathcal M_{4,q}(h)>0$, its unique pole
in this disk is simple and lies at $u=q^{-2}$. Hence
\[
 \operatorname{Res}_{u=q^{-2}}\frac{A_4(u,1/2;h)}{u^{m+1}}
 =-q^{2m}\mathcal M_{4,q}(h).
\]
Fix $0<\varepsilon<1/10$ and set $R=q^{-9/5-\varepsilon}$.
Since $q^{-2}<R<q^{-9/5}$, the residue theorem applied to
\eqref{eq:perron-first} gives
\[
 \sum_{\chi\in\mathcal C_4(g)}\chi(h)L_q(1/2,\chi)
 =q^{2m}\mathcal M_{4,q}(h)+
   \frac1{2\pi i}\oint_{|u|=R}
                  A_4(u,1/2;h)\frac{du}{u^{m+1}}.
\]
By \eqref{eq:uniform-contour}, the absolute value of the last integral
is at most
\[
 R^{-m}\sup_{|u|=R}|A_4(u,1/2;h)|
 \ll_{q,\varepsilon}q^{(9/5+\varepsilon)m}
                    |h^\ast|^{1/10+\varepsilon}|h|^\varepsilon.
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:first-input}.

label: rem:first-status
title: Remark
head: environment

label: lem:GZlength
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Each term in the first block has degree at most $N_0$, including
$P^2$ since $2B<N_0$. Expansion of the squares proves the degree bound.
For absolute coefficients, replace all signs by plus signs and remove
the Taylor cutoffs. At each prime this is coefficientwise bounded by
$e^{x+x^2/2}=\sum_{v\ge0}\alpha_vx^v$. Here
$\alpha_0=\alpha_1=\alpha_2=1$ and
$v\alpha_v=\alpha_{v-1}+\alpha_{v-2}$, so $0\le\alpha_v\le1$.
Consequently $|b_m(h)|\le\prod_{P^v\Vert h}\alpha_v\le1$.
Finally $\ell_r\le100\theta_r^{-3/4}+2$ and summing the two
geometric series gives \eqref{eq:GZlength}.
head: environment

label: lem:GZshort
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Short logarithmic upper bound

label: eq:log-upper
title: Proof
body_md:
The logarithmic-derivative argument of
\cite[Lemma~3.1]{DFL21}, before its prime-power terms are separated,
gives, with conductor degree $2m$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:log-upper}
 \log|L_q(1/2,\chi)|\le
 \operatorname{Re}\sum_{\deg f\le N}
 \frac{\Lambda(f)\chi(f)}{\deg f\sqrt{|f|}}
 e^{-\deg f/N}(1-\deg f/N)+\frac{2m}{N}.
\end{equation}
The logarithmic-derivative argument uses the shift $1/(N\log q)$
and the fact that the reciprocal zeros of the completed $L$-polynomial
have modulus $q^{1/2}$; the zero contribution is then nonpositive. For the
even characters considered here, the factor $1-q^{-s}$ is retained.
The terms of exponent at least three have absolute sum at most
\[
 \sum_P\sum_{v\ge3}\frac1{v|P|^{v/2}}
 \le\frac{-\log(1-q^{-1/2})}{3(1-q^{-1/2})}<1.
\]
Since $\chi^2$ is nonprincipal of conductor degree $2m$, its explicit
formula and the modulus $q^{1/2}$ of its reciprocal zeros imply
$|\sum_{\deg P=d}\chi(P)^2|\ll_q mq^{d/2}/d$.
The contribution of square terms of degree $d>B$ is therefore
$O_q(mq^{-B/2}/(B+1))$. For $d\le B$, replacing
$e^{-2d/N}(1-2d/N)$ by one costs $O(B/N)$, using
$\#\{P:\deg P=d\}\le q^d/d$. Hence, for $N\ge2B$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:GZsquare-shortening}
 \frac12\sum_{\deg P\le N/2}
 \frac{e^{-2\deg P/N}(1-2\deg P/N)\chi(P)^2}{|P|}
 =Q_B(\chi)+O_q\left(\frac BN+\frac{mq^{-B/2}}{B+1}\right).
\end{equation}
This error tends uniformly to zero for $N=N_j$.
Also $2m/N_j=\theta_j^{-1}+o(1)$ uniformly, since
$m\theta_0^2\to\infty$. Combining these facts proves the lemma.
head: environment

label: lem:GZTaylor
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Use $|E_\ell(z)|\le e^{|z|}$ and
$|E_\ell(z)-e^z|\le e^{|z|}|z|^{\ell+1}/(\ell+1)!$.
With $n=\ell+1$, the difference in \eqref{eq:GZTaylor} is at most
\[
 \frac{e^{(|U|+|W|)/2}}{n!}
 \big((|U|/2)^n+(|W|/2)^n\big).
\]
H\"older and the preceding exponential bounds give a factor at most
$\sqrt2e^{4V+D}$ for the exponential in its $L^2$ estimate.
Also $(\mathbb E|U|^{4n})^{1/(4n)}\le8\sqrt{nV}+D$, and the same
holds for $W$, by Lemma~\ref{lem:model-bounds} and Minkowski.
The norm is therefore at most
\[
 4e^{4V+2D}
 \left(8e\sqrt{\frac{V+D^2+1}{n}}\right)^n\le e^{-\ell}.
\]
The assumed lower bound on $\ell$ proves the last inequality.
For the pointwise statement, the relative error is at most
$e^K(eK/(2n))^n\le e^{-2\ell}$.
head: environment

label: prop:GZlater
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: eq:GZdegreecheck
title: Proof
body_md:
On $\mathcal B_n$ use the shorter scale $N_{n-1}$ in
\eqref{eq:GZshort}. For $r<n$ the prime blocks are controlled, so
\eqref{eq:GZpointTaylor} majorizes their exponentials by
$|E_{\ell_r}(\mathcal P_{r,N_{n-1}}/2)|^2$, with total correction
at most $e$. Insert
\[
 1_{\mathcal B_n}\le
 \sum_{u=n}^J|\mathcal P_{n,N_u}/K_n|^{2s_n}
\]
on the set where earlier blocks are controlled. The resulting
nonnegative finite polynomial is
\[
 \prod_{r<n}|E_{\ell_r}(\mathcal P_{r,N_{n-1}}/2)|^2
 \prod_{r=0}^J|E_{\ell_r}(-\mathcal P_{r,N_J}/2)|^2
 |\mathcal P_{n,N_u}/K_n|^{2s_n}.
\]
Its monomial radical degrees are bounded by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:GZdegreecheck}
 2L+2s_nN_n\le2L+m/2<m.
\end{equation}
Extend its sum to all monic $R\in\mathcal A_{q^2}$ of degree $m$ and apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:orthog}. The expectation then factors over blocks.
The product over $r<n$ is at most $e^3$ by
\eqref{eq:GZmatched}.

In block $n$, write $Z=\mathcal P_{n,N_u}(X)$ and
$W=\mathcal P_{n,N_J}(X)$. Both variances are at most two, and
H\"older gives
\begin{align*}
 \mathbb E\{|Z|^{2s}|E_{\ell_n}(-W/2)|^2\}
 &\le(\mathbb E|Z|^{4s})^{1/2}(\mathbb E e^{2|W|})^{1/2}\\
 &\le4e^4(16s)^s.
\end{align*}
Here $\sqrt{(2s)!}\le(2s)^s$.
Each later block contributes at most $\mathbb E e^{|W|}\le4e^2<e^4$.
The prefactors from \eqref{eq:GZshort} and
\eqref{eq:GZpointTaylor} are at most $e^{2+1/\theta_{n-1}}$ and
$e$, respectively. Multiplying these estimates and summing over $u$
gives \eqref{eq:GZbadblock}.

Now $1/(9\theta_n)\le s_n\le1/(8\theta_n)$, and
$16s_n/K_n^2\le2\sqrt{\theta_n}<1$.
Writing $t=J-n$ and using $\theta_{n-1}=\theta_n/e$, the logarithm
of the scale-dependent factors is at most
\[
 \frac{e+(\log2)/9-(64+t)/18}{\theta_n}+4t
 \le-\frac{0.7}{\theta_n}-t.
\]
Indeed $e+(\log2)/9-64/18<-0.76025$ and
$\theta_n\le e^{-64}$; the remaining negative $t/(18\theta_n)$
absorbs $5t$. Summing
$(t+1)e^{-0.7/\theta_n-t}$ gives \eqref{eq:GZbadlater}.
head: environment

label: lem:GZrough
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:GZrough}
There are fixed constants $C,C'$ such that
\[
 q^{-2m}\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal C_4(g)}|L_q(1/2,\chi)|^4\ll_q m^C,
 \qquad q^{-2m}\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal C_4(g)}|M_G(\chi)|^4\ll_q m^{C'}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For the first bound, suppose
$256(1+\log(2m))\le V\le2m\log2$, put $N=\lfloor16m/V\rfloor$ and
$s=\lfloor V/64\rfloor$. Then $2sN\le m/2$,
$s\ge V/128$, and $2m/N\le V/4$. The prime-square absolute
contribution to \eqref{eq:log-upper} is at most $(1+\log(2m))/2$, and the higher
powers contribute less than one. Thus $\log|L|>V$ forces the
weighted prime sum $Z_N(\chi)$ to have real part greater than $V/2$.
Its variance is at most $1+\log(2m)$. Finite orthogonality and
Lemma~\ref{lem:model-bounds} imply, if $\mathcal N(V)$ counts
these characters,
\[
 q^{-2m}\mathcal N(V)\le
 \left(\frac{128s(1+\log(2m))}{V^2}\right)^s
 \le\left(\frac{2(1+\log(2m))}{V}\right)^{V/128}.
\]
For $V\ge2e^{2048}(1+\log(2m))$ this is at most $e^{-16V}$. Below that
threshold use $\mathcal N(V)\le q^{2m}$, and above
$2m\log2$ use $\mathcal N(V)=0$, since the factorization of the
completed $L$-polynomial gives $|L_q(1/2,\chi)|\le2^{2m}$.
Integration against $4e^{4V}\,dV$ proves a fixed polynomial bound.

For the second estimate, $4L<m$ permits the use of
Lemma~\ref{lem:orthog}. Since
$|E_\ell(-z/2)|^8\le e^{4|z|}$, its normalized average is at most
\[
 e^{4D}4^{J+1} e^{16\sum_{r=0}^JV_r}.
\]
Here $D=O(\log\log m)$, $J=O(\log\log m)$, and
$\sum V_r\le1+\log(2m)$. This is bounded by a fixed power of $m$.
head: environment

label: lem:GZinitial
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\mathcal P_{0,N_u}=Z_u+Q_B$.
Since $|Q_B|\le D=o(K_0)$, failure in the first block implies
$|Z_u|>K_0/2$ for some $u$. Take $s_0=\lfloor K_0\rfloor$.
The degree $2s_0N_0=o(m)$ permits exact finite orthogonality.
Markov and the model moment bound give
\[
 q^{-2m}|\mathcal B_0|\le
 4(J+1)\left(\frac{16(1+\log(2m))s_0}{K_0^2}\right)^{s_0}
 \le e^{-c(\log m)^{3/2}\log\log m}
\]
for some absolute $c>0$ and sufficiently large $m$.
H\"older with exponents $2,4,4$ bounds the left side of
\eqref{eq:GZinitial} by
\[
 |\mathcal B_0|^{1/2}
 \left(\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal C_4(g)}|L_q(1/2,\chi)|^4\right)^{1/4}
 \left(\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal C_4(g)}|M_G(\chi)|^4\right)^{1/4}.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:GZrough} and the preceding bound for
$|\mathcal B_0|$ now give \eqref{eq:GZinitial}.
head: environment

label: prop:GZfirst
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply \eqref{eq:first-input} to each coefficient of
\eqref{eq:GZmollifier}. By Lemma~\ref{lem:GZlength}, the total
error is
\[
 \ll_{q,\varepsilon}q^{(9/5+\varepsilon)m}
 \sum_{\deg h\le L}|h|^{-1/2}|h^\ast|^{1/10+\varepsilon}|h|^\varepsilon
 \ll q^{(9/5+\varepsilon)m+(4/5+\varepsilon)L}=o(q^{2m}),
\]
after relabeling $\varepsilon$. The normalized main term is
\[
 c_q\sum_{h,D\in\mathcal A_q}
 \frac{b_m(h)\rho(hD)}{\sqrt{|hh^\ast|}|D|^2}.
\]
For each fixed $h$, all its prime factors eventually lie in the
first block and have degree at most $B$; their weights tend to one
and $\ell_0\to\infty$. Thus $b_m(h)$ tends to the multiplicative
coefficient whose prime series is $e^{-x-\frac{x^2}{2}}$.
For dominated convergence, use the coefficient
majorant $\prod_{P^v\Vert h}\alpha_v$ from
Lemma~\ref{lem:GZlength}. Its weighted sum is finite: the local
$h$-factor is
\[
 1+\sum_{v\ge1}\alpha_v|P|^{-2\lceil v/4\rceil}
 =1+O(|P|^{-2}),
\]
where $\sum_v\alpha_v=e^{3/2}$; the $D$-sum is $\zeta_q(2)$.
At each prime the diagonal
requires the total exponent from the mollifier and the $L$-series
to be divisible by four. Formula \eqref{eq:GZlocal} then gives
exactly the local factor in \eqref{eq:GZA}.
head: environment

label: thm:GZpositive
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Proposition~\ref{prop:GZlater} and Lemma~\ref{lem:GZinitial} give
\[
 \sum_{\chi\notin\mathcal T}|L_q(1/2,\chi)M_G(\chi)|
 \le\left(\frac{e^{20-0.7e^{64}}}{(1-e^{-1})^2}+o(1)\right)q^{2m}.
\]
The constant on the right is less than $2/27\le c_qA_{4,q,G}/4$, by
\eqref{eq:cq-lower} and \eqref{eq:GZAbounds}.
Subtracting this absolute contribution from \eqref{eq:GZfirst},
and taking $m$ sufficiently large, yields
\[
 \left|\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal T}L_q(1/2,\chi)M_G(\chi)\right|
 \ge\tfrac12c_qA_{4,q,G}q^{2m}.
\]
Each nonzero summand on $\mathcal T$ has modulus at most
$e^{1/\theta_J+3}$ by \eqref{eq:GZgood}, and characters with
zero central value contribute zero. The triangle inequality gives
\[
 N_4(g)\ge\frac{c_qA_{4,q,G}}{2e^{1/\theta_J+3}}q^{2m}
 \ge\frac{c_qA_{4,q,G}}{2e^{e^{65}+3}}q^{2m}.
\]
Divide by $|\mathcal C_4(g)|\sim c_qq^{2m}$. Finally
$e^{65}+3+\log2<e^{66}$ proves the last inequality in
\eqref{eq:GZpositive}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The proof requires the uniform twist dependence in
Theorem~\ref{input:first} and the absolute exceptional-set estimates.
A sharp mollified second-moment bound is not needed.
head: environment

label: sextic:parameterization
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
A base-field prime supports a local character of exact order six
precisely when its degree is even.  It then splits as
$P=\pi\pi^\sigma$ over $\mathbb F_Q$, and the two choices $\pi,\pi^\sigma$
give its two local characters of exact order six.  Condition
\eqref{sextic:conductor} excludes local order two and local order three
at ramified primes.  Independent local choices give the parameterization,
including $(F,F^\sigma)=1$; see \cite[Lemma~3.6]{Lin}.
For $a\in\mathbb F_q^\times$, its sextic symbol is one since $q-1$ divides
$(Q^{\deg\pi}-1)/6$.  Thus the characters are even and infinity is
unramified.  Riemann--Hurwitz gives
$2g-2=-12+5(2m)$, whereas the degree of each completed $L$-polynomial
is its conductor degree minus two.
head: environment

label: sextic:restricted-gauss
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: sextic:restricted-inclusion
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $a$ be the product of the extension-field primes dividing $h$
but not $r$.  In the notation of \cite[Section~5]{DFL25}, finite
inclusion--exclusion gives
\begin{equation}\label{sextic:restricted-inclusion}
 \widetilde\Psi_6(r,z;h)
 =(1-Q^6z^6)\sum_{E\mid a}\mu_Q(E)
                 \sum_{i=0}^5\psi_r^{(i)}(r,E,z),
\end{equation}
where $\psi_r^{(i)}(r,E,z)$ imposes $(K,r)=1$ and $E\mid K$.
Write $r=r_1r_2^2\cdots r_5^5r_6^6$ as required in
\cite[Theorem~5.3 and Corollary~5.4]{DFL25}.  Their second case applies:
$6\le6/(3-2\beta)$ throughout the stated range.  The bound is
\[
 \psi_r^{(i)}(r,E,z)
 \ll_{q,\eta}|Er|_2^\eta
 |E|_2^{7/2-3\beta}|r|_2^{3/4-\beta/2}.
\]
Since $7/2-3\beta<-1/2$, summing over $E\mid a$ costs only
$|h|_2^\eta$, after relabeling small exponents.  This proves
\eqref{sextic:restricted-bound}, retaining primes in the sixth-power
part of the original twist.  The finite decomposition in the cited
theorem has possible denominators $1-Q^7z^6$ and
$1-Q^{5\deg\pi}z^{6\deg\pi}$; the reciprocity signs are one since
$Q\equiv1\pmod{12}$.  Their zeros have radii $Q^{-7/6}$ and
$Q^{-5/6}$, respectively, proving the stated holomorphy.  Finally, on
the coprime support the Gauss sum vanishes for nonsquare-free $K$ and
otherwise has size $|K|_2^{1/2}$.  Thus absolute convergence follows
from the majorant $\zeta_Q(\beta-1/2)$ for $\beta>3/2$.
head: environment

label: sextic:tfm
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Sextic twisted first moment

title: Proof
body_md:
Periodicity and \eqref{sextic:hull} continue
$A_6(u,q^{-1/2};h)$ meromorphically to $|u|<q^{-13/7}$, with the
only pole at $u=Q^{-1}$.  Its principal part is
$\mathcal M_{6,q}(h)/(1-Qu)$ by \eqref{sextic:residue}.
For $0<\varepsilon<1/7$, move the contour in
\eqref{sextic:perron} to $|u|=q^{-13/7-\varepsilon}$.  The counting
pole contributes $q^{2m}\mathcal M_{6,q}(h)$; explicitly, the residue
of the Perron integrand there is $-q^{2m}\mathcal M_{6,q}(h)$.
The remaining integral is bounded using \eqref{sextic:contour-bound},
which proves the error term.  The Euler product follows from the
geometric series at each prime.
head: environment

label: sextic:first-moment
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $h=1$ in Theorem~\ref{sextic:tfm}. Then $h^\ast=1$, and
\eqref{sextic:main} gives the stated constant. Its Euler product
converges absolutely and has positive local factors.
head: environment

label: sextic:twist-length
title: Remark
head: environment

label: sextic:mollified-first
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Insert \eqref{sextic:tfm-formula} into \eqref{sextic:length}.
The total error is $o(q^{2m})$ by \eqref{sextic:summed-error}.
For fixed $h$, its primes eventually lie in the first block below $B$,
the weights tend to one, and the cutoffs tend to infinity.  The
coefficient limit therefore has local series $e^{-x-\frac{x^2}{2}}$.
The absolute coefficient majorant from Lemma~\ref{lem:GZlength} has
local coefficients $\alpha_v$ with $\sum_v\alpha_v=e^{3/2}$.  In the
main term its local $h$-sum is
\[
 1+\sum_{v\ge1}\alpha_v|P|^{-3\lceil v/6\rceil}
 =1+O(|P|^{-3}),
\]
and the remaining $A$-sum is bounded by $\zeta_q(3)$.  Dominated
convergence applies.  The total exponent of $fh$ must be divisible
by six; selecting those coefficients in \eqref{sextic:local-series}
gives precisely \eqref{sextic:arithmetic}.
head: environment

label: sextic:positive
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{sextic:bad-later} and \eqref{sextic:bad-initial},
\[
 \sum_{\chi\notin\mathcal T^{(6)}}
        |L_q(1/2,\chi)M_{6,G}(\chi)|
 \le\left(\frac{e^{20-0.7e^{64}}}{(1-e^{-1})^2}+o(1)\right)q^{2m}.
\]
The explicit constant is less than $c_qA_{6,q,G}/4$, since
$c_q\ge64/125$ and $A_{6,q,G}>1$.
Subtract this absolute contribution from \eqref{sextic:first}.
For sufficiently large $m$,
\[
 \left|\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal T^{(6)}}
        L_q(1/2,\chi)M_{6,G}(\chi)\right|
 \ge\tfrac12c_qA_{6,q,G}q^{2m}.
\]
A zero central value contributes zero.  Every other summand on the
good set has modulus at most $ e^{\theta_J^{-1}+3}$ by
\eqref{sextic:good}.  The triangle inequality gives
\[
 N_6(m)\ge\frac{c_qA_{6,q,G}}{2 e^{\theta_J^{-1}+3}}q^{2m}
          \ge\frac{c_qA_{6,q,G}}{2 e^{e^{65}+3}}q^{2m}.
\]
Divide by \eqref{sextic:count}.  The final inequality follows from
$e^{65}+3+\log2<e^{66}$.
head: environment

label: cubic:orthog
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Cubic reciprocity gives
$\chi_R(f)\overline{\chi_R(h)}=\left(\frac{R}{fh^2}\right)_3$.
Monic polynomials of degree $m$ are uniformly distributed modulo
$fh^2$. The complete sum vanishes unless $fh^2$ is a cube; in the
principal case it is the proportion of invertible residue classes.
Since $fh$ and $fh^2$ have the same radical, this proportion is
$\phi_Q(fh)/|fh|_2$. Finally, $\deg(fh^2)\le3D$ for the monomials
arising from $|H|^2$.
head: environment

label: cubic:twisted
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: David, Florea, and Lal\'in

title: Proof
body_md:
This is \cite[Proposition~8.1]{DFL21} in our notation. To identify the
constant, the local factor for $P\nmid h$ in the $A$-sum is
\[
 F_P=1+\frac{\rho_P|P|^{-3/2}}{1-|P|^{-3/2}}.
\]
For $P\mid h$, the correction relative to $F_P$ is
$\rho_P/(1-(1-\rho_P)|P|^{-3/2})$. It equals one at odd-degree
primes and
\[
 \frac1{1+2|P|^{-1}(1-|P|^{-3/2})}
\]
at even-degree primes. This is the factor in
\cite[(8.15)]{DFL21}. Since $\sqrt{|h^\ast|}=|C|\sqrt{|S|}$,
multiplying by $c_q\prod_PF_P$ gives the normalization in
\cite[(8.14)]{DFL21}.
head: environment

label: cubic:first
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For sufficiently large $g$, \eqref{cubic:length} gives $L<g/20$,
so Proposition~\ref{cubic:twisted} applies to every twist. The total
error is
\[
 q^{7g/8+\varepsilon g}
 \sum_{\deg h\le L}|b_m(h)||h|^{-1/4}
 \ll_q q^{7g/8+3L/4+\varepsilon g}
 \ll_q q^{(73/80+\varepsilon)g}=o(q^{2m}).
\]
The normalized main term is
\[
 c_q\sum_{h,A\in\mathcal A_q}
 \frac{b_m(h)\rho(hA)}{\sqrt{|hh^\ast|}\,|A|^{3/2}}.
\]
Dominated convergence follows from
\[
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal A_q}\frac{H(h)}{\sqrt{|hh^\ast|}}
 =\prod_P\left(1+\sum_{v\ge1}
 H(P^v)|P|^{-3\lceil v/3\rceil/2}\right)<\infty
\]
and the absolute convergence of $\zeta_q(3/2)$.
At each prime, the total exponent in $h$ and the $L$-series must be
divisible by three. By \eqref{cubic:limit-coefficients} and
\eqref{eq:GZlocal}, the local sum is
\[
 1+\rho_P\sum_{k\ge1}
    \left(\sum_{v=0}^{3k}b_\infty(P^v)\right)|P|^{-3k/2}
 =1+\rho_P\sum_{k\ge1}d_{3k}|P|^{-3k/2}.
\]
Multiplication gives \eqref{cubic:mollified-first}.
head: environment

label: cubic:exceptional
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: cubic:degree-budget
title: Proof
body_md:
For $n\ge1$, put $s_n=\lfloor1/(8\theta_n)\rfloor$. On
$\mathcal B_n^{(3)}$, apply \eqref{cubic:short-block} at scale
$N_{n-1}$ and majorize the earlier exponentials by their Taylor
polynomials. For $u\ge n$, the resulting modulus square is that of
\begin{align*}
 H_{n,u}(\chi)={}&
 \left(\frac{\mathcal P^{(3)}_{n,N_u}(\chi)}{K_n}\right)^{s_n}
 \prod_{r<n}E_{\ell_r}\!\left(
           \frac{\mathcal P^{(3)}_{r,N_{n-1}}(\chi)}2\right)
 \prod_{r=0}^J E_{\ell_r}\!\left(
          -\frac{\mathcal P^{(3)}_{r,N_J}(\chi)}2\right).
\end{align*}
Its degree $D$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{cubic:degree-budget}
 D\le s_nN_n+L,\qquad
 3D\le\frac{3m}{4}+3L<0.750611m<m.
\end{equation}
Thus \eqref{cubic:finite-average} applies after the indicator is
bounded by $\sum_{u=n}^J|\mathcal P^{(3)}_{n,N_u}/K_n|^{2s_n}$.

For the preceding blocks, the common prime-square term cancels,
and the total variance of the difference of prime weights is at
most four. The argument for \eqref{eq:GZmatched} bounds their
product of expectations by $e^3$. In block $n$, the two prime sums
have variance at most two, and the moment and exponential bounds
give
\[
 \mathbb E\left\{|Z|^{2s_n}|E_{\ell_n}(-W/2)|^2\right\}
 \le4e^4(16s_n)^{s_n}.
\]
Each subsequent block contributes at most $4e^2<e^4$. Consequently,
\begin{align}\label{cubic:single-block}
 q^{-2m}\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal B_n^{(3)}}
        |L_q(1/2,\chi)M_{3,G}(\chi)|
 \le{}&e^{20}(J-n+1)e^{\theta_{n-1}^{-1}+4(J-n)}
          \left(\frac{16s_n}{K_n^2}\right)^{s_n}.
\end{align}
This is the same bound as \eqref{eq:GZbadblock}.
Writing $t=J-n$, the inequalities
$\theta_n=\theta_Je^{-t}$ and $s_n\ge1/(9\theta_n)$ give
\[
 \theta_{n-1}^{-1}+4t+s_n\log\frac{16s_n}{K_n^2}
 \le\frac{e+(\log2)/9-(64+t)/18}{\theta_n}+4t
 \le-\frac{0.7}{\theta_n}-t.
\]
Here $e+(\log2)/9-64/18<-0.7602$.
Summing \eqref{cubic:single-block} over $n\ge1$ yields the first
term in \eqref{cubic:exceptional-bound}.

For the initial block, take $s_0=\lceil K_0\rceil$.
Since $K_0=(\log m)^{3/2}$ and $3s_0N_0=o(m)$,
finite orthogonality and the bound $V_0\le3\log m$ imply
\begin{equation}\label{cubic:initial-count}
 q^{-2m}|\mathcal B_0^{(3)}|
 \le4(J+1)\left(\frac{12s_0\log m}{K_0^2}\right)^{s_0}
 \le e^{-c(\log m)^{3/2}\log\log m}
\end{equation}
for some absolute $c>0$.
The polynomial inside the modulus square representing $|M_{3,G}|^4$
has degree at most $2L$. Since $6L<m$, another application of
\eqref{cubic:finite-average} gives
\begin{equation}\label{cubic:mollifier-fourth}
 q^{-2m}\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal C_3(g)}|M_{3,G}(\chi)|^4
 \le4^{J+1}e^{48\log m+32J}\ll m^{50}.
\end{equation}
H\"older's inequality, \eqref{cubic:fourth}, and
\eqref{cubic:initial-count}--\eqref{cubic:mollifier-fourth} now give
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{\chi\in\mathcal B_0^{(3)}}|L_q(1/2,\chi)M_{3,G}(\chi)|
 &\le |\mathcal B_0^{(3)}|^{1/2}
 \left(\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal C_3(g)}|L_q(1/2,\chi)|^4\right)^{1/4}
 \left(\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal C_3(g)}|M_{3,G}(\chi)|^4\right)^{1/4}\\
 &\ll_{q,A}q^{2m}m^{-A}.
\end{align*}
This proves \eqref{cubic:exceptional-bound}.
head: environment

label: cubic:positive
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The explicit exceptional-set constant is bounded by
\[
 \frac{e^{20}}{(1-e^{-1})^2}e^{-0.7e^{64}}
 <\frac18\cdot\frac{64}{125}<\frac18c_qA_{3,q,G}.
\]
Subtracting \eqref{cubic:exceptional-bound} from
\eqref{cubic:mollified-first} therefore gives, for sufficiently
large $m$,
\[
 \left|\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal T^{(3)}}
                L_q(1/2,\chi)M_{3,G}(\chi)\right|
 \ge\frac12c_qA_{3,q,G}q^{2m}.
\]
By \eqref{cubic:pointwise}, every nonzero summand has modulus at
most $ e^{e^{65}+3}$. The triangle inequality and
\eqref{cubic:count} give \eqref{cubic:positive-bound}.
head: environment
